annotations.text:
The change that matters most.

Today "Required Pressure" names two different quantities: the 0.25 bar headline tile (pipe drop) and the 25.3 bar figure at the bottom of the page (pipe drop + machine losses). They differ by 100x and share a label.

Here the headline is the number you act on — what to set the machine to — with the line demand shown as its supporting arithmetic.

Today the panel says "Process Optimized — no critical warnings detected" while, further down, scorch risk reads moderate and the material is arriving 12 C below the set point.

One strip, worst first, replaces the standing reassurance.

Estimated vs measured.

The nucleation factor and heat of reaction are calibrated assumptions. Today that is a paragraph of prose at the foot of one card.

A dotted underline marks every figure resting on an assumption, with one legend explaining it — so it reads the same wherever it appears.

Four conditional blocks currently appear and vanish depending on which optional fields were filled, so the page reflows and nothing sits where you last saw it.

Here the sections are fixed slots. An unmodelled one keeps its place and says what to enter to switch it on (see "Mould fill").

Two fixes in the chart card.

The live chart overflows its container — the legend is clipped mid-word and the plot runs past the right edge, stopping at 400 mm on a 500 mm pipe.

And the same three pressures are printed twice: once as tiles under the chart, again as rows beneath. Stated once here.

Before a run, the form is a 300px column beside 900px of empty panel.

Giving it the width lets the material and machine choices show what they resolve to — the CSV row's viscosity, density and gel time, the machine's operating window — which is how you catch a wrong database row before running anything.

After a run it collapses to the rail shown on the results board.

The optional inputs sit behind a control reading "OPTIONAL (chevron) Shop conditions & part", wrapped across two lines.

They are a named section here, open, with one line saying what each pair switches on.

At 390px the header currently overlaps: "PU Optimizer" collides with the Documentation and GitHub links.

And every section renders expanded, making the results page 5551px tall — roughly seven screens of scrolling to reach the machine check.

Three defects the screenshots turned up, all in ResultsDisplay.tsx, none of them design questions:

1. "Viscosity at 12.901331283799657 C" — the label interpolates the raw float.

2. Water-blown foam has GWP 0, and the row is guarded by {gwp_per_kg && ...}. Zero is falsy, so React renders a bare "0" and the GWP row is hidden in exactly the case where the value is best. heat_generated_w has the same guard.

3. When material temperature equals the reference temperature, the two viscosity rows are identical: "Viscosity at 25 C 447.57 cP" printed twice.
